title: CUDA driver/library mismatch breaks 2 ImageNet-C data tests
description:
Two tests fail when moving tensors to CUDA via pin_memory: tests/test_imagenet_c_data.py::test_imagenet_c_loader_and_suite_metadata and ::test_clean_imagenet_loader_uses_canonical_class_indices. Failure is torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: out of memory on data.pin_memory().

## Context
Host has an NVIDIA driver/library version mismatch: kernel module NVRM 595.58.03 (/proc/driver/nvidia/version) vs userspace NVML library 595.71 (nvidia-smi reports 'Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch'). torch.cuda.is_available() returns True but allocations fail. Same torch 2.12.0 as the original .venv-dememte-e5y, so this is NOT caused by the uv migration. The other 76 CPU-only tests pass. These experiments ran fine before, so the driver state may have changed/be intentional on this host.
acceptance_criteria: nvidia-smi works (no NVML mismatch) AND 'uv run pytest -q tests/test_imagenet_c_data.py' passes. Likely fixed by a host reboot or aligning the NVIDIA kernel module with the userspace libs. Workaround: run those tests on CPU.
notes: CI (lint+smoke) is intentionally torch-free so it stays green regardless of host GPU/driver state.
